Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on this account, and with me is Marcus our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Sarah: Good, thanks. Busy day but excited to see the demo.
[00:10] Marcus: Cool, we'll jump in. Quick agenda: show Hosted API for embeddings, the rerank endpoint and then a quick look at Console/Optimize suggestions for batching and cost.
[00:20] Tom: Sounds good, we mostly care about improving our site search relevance for product pages and keeping p99 latency under 300ms.
[00:30] Marcus: Great, that's helpful. Just to qualify — what's your current stack for embeddings? Are you storing vectors in Pinecone or OpenSearch?
[00:40] Priya: We're using OpenSearch today for vector store, and a mix of our own TF-IDF features. We tried a vendor for embeddings but the quality was inconsistent.
[00:52] Lena: Understood. Quick note: Redwood Hosted API can handle embeddings + rerank in two calls or via our combined rerank endpoint which does an embed + re-rank in one flow. For production scale you'd typically precompute embeddings for your catalog and then call the rerank endpoint to re-score candidate lists.
[01:10] Marcus: (screen share) Ok I'm on the Console — here's the Embeddings endpoint docs, sample request. The important part is vector dimension compatibility and we expose multiple model choices.
[01:25] Sarah: When you say model choices, can we pick smaller models for cost? We have 50M monthly queries — cost matters.
[01:35] Marcus: Yes, you can choose different models. The Console shows recommended model by workload; Optimize also gives quantization / batch sizing suggestions. For example we recommend a 1536-d embed model for catalog search, but if you need lower cost there's a 768-d variant with slightly lower recall.
[01:55] Tom: And latency for the rerank call — is that calling the LM to score re-ranked candidates? We need sub-300 for p99, ideally 200.
[02:05] Marcus: Rerank is a lightweight scoring pass. If you're sending top-K candidates (say top 50) the token cost is small and typical latency on Hosted is around 80–150ms for the rerank-only call, depending on model and sequence length. For combined embed+rerank it can be ~200–300ms. If you need tighter SLOs we can propose Dedicated capacity and pinned model instances.
[02:25] Sarah: Dedicated — that's reserved GPUs, right? Do we have to commit annually?
[02:30] Lena: There are commit options, monthly or annual reserved pools. We can sketch costs in the pricing doc. Also we offer autoscaling burst so you don't overprovision for spiky traffic.
[02:40] Priya: How do you handle caching? Would we be able to cache prefix embeddings?
[02:45] Marcus: Yes, we have prefix/KV cache in the runtime, though my slide here says K V cash in the notes cause the auto transcript hates K V cache. It speeds up repeated calls and reduces token cost.
[02:55] Tom: Ok good. On security, we need SSO + SAML, SOC2, and KMS integration for keys — do you have that?
[03:05] Lena: Yes, we support SSO/SAML, RBAC via Console, and KMS for Private + Dedicated. Hosted customers can use customer-managed keys in our enterprise package. We'll share the SOC2 whitepaper and security pack after the call.
[03:18] Sarah: Great. Can you show the rerank API request and a real example?
[03:22] Marcus: Sure — switching to the sample notebook. Here's a basic rerank request: you pass the user query, an array of candidate documents (we accept text or structured doc snippets), and we return scored candidates with explain metadata if enabled.
[03:38] [03:39] Speaker 1 (auto): trans phrase error
[03:41] Marcus: The explain metadata is lightweight — a short token-level score and matching highlights. For long docs we recommend pre-truncating to the most relevant passages before sending.
[03:55] Priya: Could you show an example with our product titles?
[03:58] Marcus: Yep, using a mocked dataset — query: "wireless earbuds noise cancellation". Candidates: "Acme AirBuds 2", "Acme SoundLite", "Acme Studio Pro". The rerank returns scores — the model correctly upweights AirBuds 2 because the feature list mentions ANC.
[04:20] Tom: The scores — are they probabilistic? How should we combine them with existing signal (sales rank, CTR)?
[04:28] Marcus: Scores are normalized floats. Typical approach: weighted linear combination with your existing heuristics. Optimize can help you tune the weight using a small eval set. We can show a quick grid search in the notebook.
[04:40] Sarah: What's the cost shape — embedding store + rerank calls — anything to watch for?
[04:45] Marcus: Embedding cost is per-vector generation, rerank is per-token. The big lever is precomputing catalog embeddings and only calling embed at inference for user queries or cold items. Also batching multiple queries reduces overhead. Optimize will recommend batch sizes and model changes to balance quality and unit cost.
[04:59] Priya: Any pitfalls for vector similarity vs rerank? Sometimes vector search returns poor order even if recall is ok.
[05:05] Marcus: Right — vector recall gets candidates, rerank is where the semantic scoring happens on the full query+candidate text to get relevance. We often see best results when vector retrieval gives top 100 and rerank reduces to top 10.
[05:20] Tom: For the POC what do you need from us?
[05:24] Lena: Ideally a sample product catalog (anonymized) and 1–2 weeks of query logs plus evaluation queries and expected top results. Marcus will run a baseline with hosted endpoints and share the rerank notebook.
[05:36] Tom: Ok we can get that. Concern on data residency — some of our users in EU need data to stay in EU region. Is region pinning possible?
[05:45] Lena: Yes, Hosted supports region-restricted routing, and Dedicated/Private gives you full control. We'll include region options in the follow-up.
[05:54] Sarah: Any mention of competitors? We were comparing to Pinecone + our in-house re-ranker and also looked at Anthropic for rerank.
[06:02] Lena: We often see teams use Pinecone for vector store + a separate model for rerank; Redwood tries to unify that with the rerank endpoint so you don't need glue code.
[06:12] Marcus: Quick demo note — here's the actual API payload and a live response. Sorry if the transcript clips some of the long code blocks, but file will be attached.
[06:25] Speaker 2 (auto): uh-huh
[06:26] Marcus: See response: candidates list with scores 0.87, 0.62, 0.45 — and a small explanation field showing matched tokens.
[06:35] Priya: Looks promising. What SLA do you offer for Hosted?
[06:39] Lena: Hosted has a best-effort SLA with support SLAs for paid tiers; Dedicated has contractual uptime SLOs. We'll include SLA tiers in the pricing doc.
[06:48] Tom: About debugging — if we see regressions after a model update, how do we trace?
[06:53] Marcus: Console has per-route dashboards, token-level traces, and you can pin older model variants. Optimize also includes quality monitoring tied to your eval sets and will raise regression alerts.
[07:06] Sarah: That would be very useful.
[07:09] Marcus: Final quick note: when you run the POC we'll set up a test route, point your dev environment, and run a 1-week traffic mirror. We'll collect metrics and then recommend Dedicated vs Hosted based on cost/latency.
